Sana (Marketing): Hey runtime team — we need a reproducibility bundle + a quick sanity pass on benchmark numbers for the launch post. Can you take this on?
Mike (Runtime Eng): Sure. Narrow it down for us: which model variants, quantized or fp16, and what metrics do you actually need?
Sana (Marketing): Primary: throughput (tokens/sec), 50/95/99 latencies, cold-start penalty (first request), and unit cost estimate. We want the hosted snapshot for redwood-14b and a quantized 14b-INT8 variant. Also one representative open model for comparison.
Sana (Marketing): Target cohorts: 1) short chat (<=64 tokens), 2) single-turn generation (512 tokens), 3) long-context (2k tokens).
Ben (Runtime Eng): Ok. For reproducibility bundle we need sample payloads, RNG seeds, and warmup policy. Can you paste a small payload and exact sampling settings?
Sana (Marketing): Pasted sample payloads below — please run against the same prompt set used for the marketing claims. Label outputs with the run id we share.
Sana (Marketing): ```
{
  "model": "redwood-14b",
  "input": "Summarize the following product doc in 3 bullets...",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "top_p": 0.95
}
```
Sana (Marketing): Sampling settings: temp 0.2, top_p 0.95, deterministic seed 42 for evals. We'll want both streaming and non-stream batch runs for throughput.
Mike (Runtime Eng): Got it. We'll run on dedicated staging pool to avoid noisy neighbors. Proposal: 3 cohorts x 1k requests each, 3 repeats, warmup 50 requests per worker, measure p50/p95/p99 and cold-start from an idle node. Is that acceptable?
Sana (Marketing): Yes, that sounds right. Can you also include quantized warmup behavior (INT8) — marketing wants to call out any additional warmup cost.
Ben (Runtime Eng): We'll include: (a) baseline fp16 run, (b) quantized INT8 run with recommended warmup, (c) fallback policy trace if quantized hits numeric regressions. We'll attach traces and raw logs.
Soledad (Data Ops): For the reproducibility bundle I'll need the prompt set filename and the matching sample index map. Sana, can you drop the prompt set link + a short description of the curation?
Sana (Marketing): Link: https://internal.storage/redwood/launch/prompts-v3.txt — curated from product docs + user queries, ~120 prompts, stratified by length.
Ben (Runtime Eng): ETA: initial runs by Thursday EOD. If regressions or flaky runs, we'll schedule reruns Friday morning. We'll post artifacts to the launch bench folder and tag marketing.
runtime-ci-bot: Run queued: bench-run/1714239999-1, allocating staging-x1. Status: queued. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sana (Marketing): Amazing — please include a short readme in the bundle with: exact command lines, docker image tags, and the random seeds used. Marketing will need the p95 delta callouts for the launch deck.
Mike (Runtime Eng): Will do. Quick question: do you want cost normalized to our current pricing snapshot or raw GPU seconds + effective tokens?
Sana (Marketing): Both please. Marketing wants a headline-friendly $/1k tokens and a technical appendix with raw GPU-seconds and batch sizes.
Ben (Runtime Eng): Understood. We'll add a small notebook that recreates the headline numbers from raw logs.
Soledad (Data Ops): I'll coordinate the artifact upload and add checksums. Please ping me when the runs complete.
Sana (Marketing): Thanks team — tagging #launch-2026 in the headers of the bundle. If all looks good we'll cut the copy on Monday. :rocket: 
Mike (Runtime Eng): Copy. We'll update this thread with the artifact links when ready.
Sana (Marketing): Thanks — appreciate the fast turn. :pray:
